top10.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.  
Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway.
**fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.
## Install
```sh
npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything      # or: cargo install fast-anything
```
Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)).
## Use
```sh
fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py     # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R
```
Or step by step:
| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scan --  ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are |
| `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` |
| `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call |
| `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) |
| `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs |
| `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR |
| `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents |
`--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use.
## Proof, not vibes
That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time.
## Results
Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples).
| app | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** |
| TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** |

English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Benchmarks](#real-world-benchmarks) · [MCP Tools](#the-5-mcp-tools) · [Analysis Report](docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
**`agy-fast`** is a zero-dependency, policy-compliant local [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) plugin for **Google Antigravity** (CLI `agy`, Desktop 2.0, and IDE). It cuts agent wall-clock latency, billable token quota, and upload traffic by consolidating high-frequency searches, multi-language symbol outlines, atomic multi-file edits, and build/test checks into batched local calls—and injecting a sub-50 ms workspace snapshot once per session—without altering Antigravity's native UI, diff viewer, modified-files list, checkpoints, or safety checks.
| LLM Turns / 10 Actions | Est. Billable Quota | Tool-Return Upload | Spills & Native UI Impact |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **-33.7%**  `-38.2%` ≥150k ctx · `-58.8%` subagents  | **-31.5%**  `-36.5%` ≥150k ctx · `-54.0%` subagents  | **-39.7%**  `-53.7%` uncached fresh input  | **0**  `≤8.8 KB` inline cap · Native diff & UI untouched  |
## Quick Start
**Requirements:** **Node.js >= 20** (no `npm install` needed — pre-built, unminified zero-dependency ESM bundles are included in `dist/`). Optional: [`ripgrep` (`rg`)](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) for faster code search (automatically falls back to pure Node.js when absent).
### One-Command Install (Recommended)
Installs runtime files to `~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast`, runs `agy plugin validate --strict` and `agy plugin enable agy-fast` when `agy` is installed, and verifies both the MCP server and `SessionStart` hook live:
**macOS / Linux:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.sh | sh
```
**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

top10.descricao_en: Render Anything Engine: tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games as React and TypeScript, rendered on your own GPU. Rust + Bevy, macOS, Linux and Windows.
top10.readme:
raea 
  Render Anything Engine   (for Anyone)  
  Tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games, written as React and TypeScript 
  (the code your AI already writes) and rendered on your own GPU, faster than they play.
   raea.io  ·
   Made in raea  ·
   Why raea  ·
   Docs  ·
   Releases 
---
> **0.1.6** (17 November 2026) is the latest release: the engine and the desktop app on macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux
> (x86_64) and, newest and least tested, Windows 10 and 11 (x86_64). raea is young and moves fast, with a release most
> days since 0.1.1 on 11 November: expect rough edges, and tell us what you hit in an
> [issue](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/issues), or from your agent with `raea bug`.
## The app
The raea app is where you make video, 3D and games with your AI. You ask in a chat; your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi
or a local model) writes the raea code and renders it; what it makes lands in the project's feed, where you watch it,
scrub it, mark it up and send it back with notes. Download it from [raea.io](https://raea.io) for the Mac, Windows or
Linux. It tells you when a new version is out; on the Mac it updates itself.
New to the app? **[Watch the tutorial](https://media.raea.io/#goose-learns-raea)** (5:50).
What the app does now:
- **The chat comes first** (0.1.5): your projects in a rail, the conversation in the middle, and `/goal` to keep an
  agent going until a condition you set holds.
- **A timeline you edit by hand** (0.1.4): trim, split and move clips, speed curves, freeze frames and keys, the way
  CapCut works, under every film, sound and scene.
- **Scenes you walk around in** (0.1.3): your agent posts a 3D scene and you walk through it, pin comments in it and
  move its parts by hand; every change is written into the scene's own code.
- **Index** (0.1.5): your folders, drives and Apple Photos made searchable by what's in them, on your Mac. On an M5 Pro,
  10,000 pictures were searchable in under a minute.
- **Review** (0.1.6): each project has a Review tab, every comment you leave reaches the agent, and export is one
  window.
- **Lighter** (0.1.6): the window gives back memory it's finished with and rests when nothing changes, 34% less CPU
  at rest.
The app and the engine are free. Pro adds cloud storage, search across your computers and publishing; Team puts up to
five people on one plan ([pricing](https://raea.io/pricing/)). Each release's notes are on the
[releases page](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea

top10.readme:
# Logo Design Skill for Claude & AI Agents
[ ](https://github.com/sponsors/kaankiziltug) [ ](https://github.com/kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill/actions/workflows/test.yml) [ ](#)
A comprehensive **logo-design skill** that turns Claude — or any agent that supports Agent Skills, such as Gemini
CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor or GitHub Copilot — into a disciplined identity designer, from the first brief to
production-ready SVG files and brand guidelines.
- **Principles & process** — discovery and briefs, word mapping, choosing the right mark type, concepting,
  geometric construction, optical corrections (overshoot, bone effect, irradiation…), colour, typography, lockups,
  testing, presentation, delivery, redesigns and identity systems.
- **A reference library of 1,400+ real-world SVG logos**, each visually classified by mark type, technique,
  geometry, subject, typography, mood and industry — searchable from the command line and browsable in a local
  gallery. Used to study construction, map category conventions and avoid look-alikes (never to copy).
- **Dependency-free Python tools** — audit an SVG against logo principles, build concept overview sheets and test
  sheets (16 px pixel test, one-colour, reversed, squint, mirror, contexts, competitor shelf test), create client
  presentation boards with industry-specific mockups, render PNGs, and export a complete favicon / app-icon /
  web-manifest set.
**Contents:** [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#install) · [Examples](#examples) ·
[Tests](#what-the-tests-catch) · [Use](#use) · [What's inside](#whats-inside) · [Library](#library-at-a-glance)
---
## How it works
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Brief questions or stated assumptions] --> B[Research category conventions in the library]
    B --> C[Concepts 8–12 one-liners → build 3 in SVG]
    C --> D[Test & refine audit · 16 px · one-colour · shelf test]
    D --> E{{Checkpoint show concepts, recommend, stop}}
    E -- "you pick a direction and ask for the kit" --> F[Kit colour · lockups · board · icons · guidelines]
    E -- "you want changes" --> C
```
The skill always **stops at the checkpoint**: it shows the concepts as one overview image with a recommendation and
offers the full kit. Nothing else is produced until you choose a direction — the kit is most of the work and only
makes sense for an approved idea.
---

/plugin install logo-desi
